full_text_en:
Tianjin Goubuli Baozi Catering (Group) Co., Ltd. v. Harbin Tianlongge Restaurant and Gao Yuan — dispute over infringement of trademark right (retrial)

Original Appellant: Tianjin Goubuli Baozi Catering (Group) Co., Ltd.

Legal Representative: Ding Chengzhi, General Manager.

Original Appellee: Harbin Tianlongge Restaurant, Heilongjiang Province.

Legal Representative: Tao De, Manager.

Original Appellee: Gao Yuan, male, 34 years old, residing in Tianjin.

The Original Appellant, Tianjin Goubuli Baozi Catering (Group) Co., Ltd., dissatisfied with the final judgment of the Harbin Intermediate People's Court in the case of Tianjin Goubuli Baozi Catering (Group) Co., Ltd. v. Harbin Tianlongge Restaurant and Gao Yuan concerning a trademark infringement dispute, applied to the Heilongjiang High People's Court for a retrial pursuant to Article 178 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC. On December 14, 1994, the High People's Court decided by Civil Ruling (1994) Hei Shen Jing Jian Zi No. 93 to take over the case for trial.

Facts found and judgments rendered in the first and second instance:

In July 1980, Tianjin Goubuli Baozi Catering (Group) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Goubuli Baozi Catering Company) obtained Trademark Registration Certificate No. 138850 for the Goubuli brand from the State Administration for Industry and Commerce of the PRC. On January 7, 1991, Dong Fengli, agent ad litem of the defendant Gao Yuan, and Tao De, the legal representative of the defendant Harbin Tianlongge Restaurant (hereinafter referred to as Tianlongge Restaurant), entered into a cooperation agreement. In March 1991, after the defendant Tianlongge Restaurant commenced business, it hung a signboard above its door with the content "Authentic Tianjin Goubuli Baozi, Fourth Generation Descendant Gao Yaolin, Fifth Generation Descendant Gao Yuan", and engaged Gao Yuan as the chef for the restaurant's noodles and filling. The restaurant began selling baozi from March 1991.

After trial, the Xiangfang District People's Court of Harbin held that the acts of the two defendants in entering into the cooperation agreement and producing and hanging the said signboard were for the purpose of publicizing the personal identities of Gao Yaolin and Gao Yuan as the fourth and fifth generation descendants of Gao Guiyou, the founder of "Goubuli", and did not constitute using a trademark identical or similar to the plaintiff's registered trademark, or a product name or trade dress identical or similar to that of the plaintiff's registered trademark, on baozi or similar goods. Therefore, the plaintiff's claim that the two defendants had infringed its right to use the registered trademark was unsupported by sufficient evidence. The plaintiff's requests for the defendants to cease the infringement, publish an apology in newspapers, and compensate for economic losses were not sustained. The judgment dismissed the plaintiff's claims.

Goubuli Baozi Catering Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed on the grounds that the original judgment had unclear factual findings, misapplication of law, and was contrary to the principle of fairness. After trial, the Harbin Intermediate People's Court held that the facts of the case were clear; the signboard produced and hung by the appellees Gao Yuan and Harbin Tianlongge Restaurant was a publicity of personal identity, not a publicity of the appellant's registered trademark, and the appellees had not used a trademark, product name, or trade dress identical or similar to the appellant's trademark on baozi or similar goods. Therefore, the evidence was insufficient to prove that the appellees had infringed the appellant's trademark right, and the appellant's appeal requests were not supported. The original court's factual findings were clear and the application of law was correct. The judgment dismissed the appeal and affirmed the original judgment.

Goubuli Baozi Catering Company remained dissatisfied and, on the ground that Tianlongge Restaurant and Gao Yuan had constituted trademark infringement, applied to the Heilongjiang High People's Court for a retrial.

Upon retrial, the Heilongjiang High People's Court found that the facts found by the courts of first and second instance were substantially correct. It further found that the signboard hung above the door of the appellee Tianlongge Restaurant had large characters in the middle reading "Tianjin Goubuli Baozi", with the smaller characters "Authentic" above and "Fourth Generation Descendant Gao Yaolin, Fifth Generation Descendant Gao Yuan" below, and no signboard bearing the name of Tianlongge Restaurant was hung. The appellant, Tianjin Goubuli Baozi Catering Company, had obtained a trademark registration certificate from the State Administration for Industry and Commerce in July 1980; on March 1, 1993, the State Administration for Industry and Commerce renewed the trademark for an additional ten years. During the trial of this case, upon entrustment to the State Administration for Industry and Commerce for appraisal, it was determined that the cooperation agreement entered into by Tianlongge Restaurant and Gao Yuan and the production and hanging of the aforementioned signboard constituted trademark infringement.

The Heilongjiang High People's Court held that the "Goubuli Brand" trademark is a valid trademark registered by the appellant Goubuli Baozi Catering Company with the State Administration for Industry and Commerce, and it enjoys exclusive rights as provided by law and is protected by law. Although the appellee Gao Yuan claimed to be a descendant of the founder of Goubuli Baozi, he does not have the right to use the "Goubuli" trademark, nor does he have the authority to enter into any agreement with Tianlongge Restaurant regarding the use of the "Goubuli" trademark. The purpose of the appellees Tianlongge Restaurant and Gao Yuan in producing and hanging the signboard was to operate the restaurant, not to publicize the descendants of the "Goubuli" baozi. Therefore, Tianlongge Restaurant's unauthorized production and use of the "Goubuli" trademark, without permission from Goubuli Baozi Catering Company, constitutes trademark infringement as specified in Article 38(1) of the Trademark Law of the PRC: "using a trademark identical or similar to a registered trademark on the same or similar goods without the authorization of the owner of the registered trademark," and infringes upon the exclusive right to use the trademark of Goubuli Baozi Catering Company. Pursuant to Article 134, Paragraph 1, Items (1), (7), and (10) of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC, Tianlongge Restaurant and Gao Yuan shall cease the infringement, issue an apology, and compensate for the losses caused to Goubuli Baozi Catering Company. The original judgment's characterization of the acts of Tianlongge Restaurant and Gao Yuan was legally erroneous and should be corrected. In accordance with Articles 184 and 153, Paragraph 1, Item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law, the judgment of December 28, 1994, is as follows:

1. The Civil Judgment (1993) Ha Jing Zhong Zi No. 295 of the Harbin Intermediate People's Court and the Civil Judgment (1993) Xiang Jing Chu Zi No. 37 of the Xiangfang District People's Court of Harbin are hereby vacated;

2. Tianlongge Restaurant and Gao Yuan shall cease their infringement of the registered trademark of Goubuli Baozi Catering Company, and shall immediately remove and destroy the signboard hanging in front of Tianlongge Restaurant from the date this judgment takes effect;

3. Tianlongge Restaurant and Gao Yuan shall, within 30 days from the date this judgment takes effect, publish an apology statement in a newspaper at or above the municipal level in Harbin, the contents of which shall be subject to court approval, with the costs to be borne by Tianlongge Restaurant and Gao Yuan;

4. Tianlongge Restaurant and Gao Yuan shall compensate Goubuli Baozi Catering Company in the amount of RMB 44,800 for the trademark infringement. This compensation shall be joint and several, and shall be paid within 10 days from the date the judgment takes effect; if payment is overdue, enforcement shall proceed in accordance with Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law.

The case acceptance fees for the first and second instances, totaling RMB 7,380, shall be borne jointly by Tianlongge Restaurant and Gao Yuan.
